statement: Goal parity against the hub's own bar (injection and management bound to the same native identity): full = OpenCode and Pi; injection-only = Cursor and Devin; read-only projection = Hermes via the repo plugin; native-equivalent = Claude and Codex with no repo-side path.

The goal hub's per-runtime delivery table lists six runtimes and omits Hermes, which has a working binding (repo-guards-goal section, GOAL_RUNTIME=hermes, _goal_slice fallback); an auditor reading the hub would report a false gap or rebuild an existing path.
Cursor's and Devin's injection-only adapters are not read-only: both record a turn on the bound record, which is the one write they make.

Cursor's partial goal support is an identity limit, not an adapter limit: management needs a native session identity the prompt command does not carry, so /goal-cursor fails closed for every management action and answers only a session-free packet read. No adapter should be added.

Repo-side coverage for Claude/Codex exists and is wired (speckit YAML goal handover across plan/resume/implement/complete plus the always-on goal posture row at AGENTS.md:185 and CLAUDE.md:185), but the host goal command itself is only operator-confirmed and neither .claude/settings.json nor .codex/hooks.json carries a goal registration that would break if the host changed; Codex's coverage rests on a parity assumption derived from Claude's confirmation, and there is no goal-codex.md prompt stub.

Operator cost by runtime: Cursor/Devin do not re-read a mid-session bind (no refresh, no verify/continue); Claude/Codex fail silently if the host command is absent or renamed; Hermes's cost falls on maintainers through the missing doc row; OpenCode/Pi have none.

Whether the Claude and Codex hosts actually expose a native goal command is unverified in-repo; the hub says operator-confirmed 2026-09-12 and re-checkable only against a live host. Confirming check: a live host probe.
